name: Flapjacks
summary: Small, thick South African pancakes, light and golden, stacked with butter, golden syrup and berries.
about: Flapjacks are what South Africans call small, thick pancakes — also called crumpets in many homes — made for weekend breakfasts, tea time and school cake sales.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: melted, plus a little for the pan

steps: Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a bowl and stir in the sugar.
In a jug, whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla and melted butter together.

Make a well in the flour, pour in the egg mixture and stir just until you have a smooth, thick batter that drops slowly from the spoon. A few small lumps are fine; overmixing makes them tough. Leave it for 5 minutes.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat and wipe it with a little butter. Drop in tablespoons of batter, 4 or 5 at a time, so they spread to about 8 cm.

Cook for 1½–2 minutes, until bubbles pop on the surface and the edges look dry, then flip and cook for 1 minute more, until golden and springy. Turn the heat down if they brown too fast. Keep them warm under a clean tea towel.
Serve stacked with butter, golden syrup and berries, or with jam and cream.
